profiles.name: Town of Carleton Place
profiles.blurb: Lower-tier municipality at the crossroads of Highway 7 and Highway 15, spelled Carleton Place since an 1830 post office (the settlement began as Morphy's Falls in 1819 on the Mississippi River). Village in 1870, town in 1890; motto Fidelis.
facts: Municipal office: 175 Bridge Street; council and committee work sits behind most items in the district feed.
Population 12,517 at the 2021 census — up 17.6% from 2016; the 2038 projection reaches 20,964.
Home of the oldest continuously operating Canoe Club in Canada; the Mississippi River runs through town.

profiles.name: Lanark County OPP
profiles.blurb: Ontario Provincial Police detachment policing all eight municipalities of the county — Carleton Place, Mississippi Mills, Perth, Beckwith, Montague, Drummond/North Elmsley, Tay Valley and Lanark Highlands — on contract.
facts: A detachment office operates in Carleton Place at 15 Coleman Street; the Lanark County detachment headquarters is at 75 Dufferin Street, Perth (East Region).
Community-safety discussions in the word-of-mouth column — thefts, break-ins, traffic — repeatedly cite the OPP's detachments and response practices.
Oversight sits with the Lanark County OPP Detachment Board, whose Carleton Place appointee is Councillor Dena Comley.

profiles.name: Thomas Cavanagh Construction Limited
profiles.blurb: Eastern Ontario contractor and aggregates producer — construction, asphalt, concrete, land development and homebuilding — founded in 1953 by Thomas Cavanagh with a single dump truck. More than 1,200 employees across three divisions.
facts: Head office on Highway 7 in Ashton since 1984; a concrete plant (Cavanagh Concrete) operates at 205 Industrial Avenue in Carleton Place.
Rebuilt the historic mill in Almonte as the Enerdu hydroelectric facility, completed 2018.
Founder's $1,000,000 gift to the Carleton Place & District Memorial Hospital named its emergency wing; the Thomas Cavanagh Foundation continues the giving.
